title: Data Loss During Submission
description: Student's assignment work file may be lost or corrupted during upload to the Grades Portal Web App, resulting in incomplete or unavailable submission data.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission and upload process without redundancy mechanisms.

title: Unauthorized Access to Submission Data
description: Student's submitted assignment data (work file, student id, course, timestamp) may be accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Assumes potential network interception or unauthorized system access.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Information
description: Student's personal information (student id, course) and submission details may be disclosed to unauthorized parties without proper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes potential lack of proper authentication or access controls on the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Destruction of Submitted Work
description: The submitted assignment work file may be accidentally or maliciously destroyed during processing or storage, resulting in permanent loss of student's work.
assumptions: Assumes potential system errors or malicious deletion during processing.

title: Submission System Unavailability
description: The Grades Portal Web App may be unavailable during critical submission times, preventing students from submitting their assignments.
assumptions: Assumes potential system failures, maintenance, or overload during peak submission periods.

title: Privacy Regulation Non-Compliance
description: The submission process may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student data collection, storage, and transmission.
assumptions: Assumes potential gaps in privacy controls or data handling procedures.

title: Student identifier transmitted to grading service
description: The Grades Portal Web App transmits student ID to the Assignment & Grading Service, which contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject. This enables tracking and identification of students across the system.
assumptions: Student ID is transmitted as part of the submission request

title: Processing of identified data at portal
description: The Grades Portal Web App requests and processes identified data (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) before routing to the Assignment & Grading Service. This processing of identifying information creates privacy risks.
assumptions: Portal processes student data before forwarding to grading service

title: Non-repudiation of student submissions
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives student submissions and grades. Students may be unable to deny their involvement in the submission process or the grading outcome, as the system creates evidence linking them to their submissions and grades.
assumptions: System maintains records of who submitted what and when

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role. This data enables linking of student activities across different systems and creates potential for cross-system tracking.
assumptions: Student ID is used as a key to link activities

title: Teacher's request for submissions processed without proper authorization
description: The teacher (EE3) requests the queue of submissions to review, but the system may process this request without verifying the teacher's authorization level or course ownership, potentially leading to unauthorized access to student data.
assumptions: Teacher may not have proper authorization to view all submissions

title: Teacher's request may leak sensitive student data to unauthorized parties
description: When the teacher requests the submission queue, the system may inadvertently expose sensitive student information to the teacher without proper safeguards, or the teacher may share this data with unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Teacher may not be bound by privacy obligations

title: System processes teacher's request for submissions without adequate data minimization
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes the teacher's request for submission queue, but may not apply data minimization principles, potentially exposing more data than necessary for the review purpose.
assumptions: System may return full submission details rather than minimal required information

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Information
description: Student submissions (names, work content, submission times) may be disclosed to unauthorized teachers or parties without proper authorization or access controls.

title: Loss of Student Submission Data
description: Student submission data may be lost or not properly transmitted to the teacher during the data flow from portal to teacher.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Display
description: The display of student submissions to teachers may have unintended consequences, such as teachers seeing more information than intended or data being used for purposes other than educational assessment.

title: Lack of authentication for grade entry
description: The Grades Portal Web App may lack proper authentication mechanisms to verify the identity of the teacher before allowing grade and feedback entry, potentially allowing unauthorized individuals to record grades.
assumptions: Assumes the system should require teacher authentication before allowing grade entry.

title: Inadequate access control for student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may have insufficient access controls to ensure only authorized teachers can view and modify specific students' grades and feedback, potentially exposing student information to unauthorized personnel.
assumptions: Assumes the system should restrict access based on teacher-student relationships.

title: Non-repudiation of grade entries
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not provide adequate non-repudiation mechanisms to ensure that grade entries can be attributed to the specific teacher who made them, potentially allowing teachers to deny having recorded certain grades.
assumptions: Assumes the system should provide audit trails and digital signatures for grade entries.

title: Data integrity during grade entry
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not adequately protect the integrity of grade and feedback data during transmission and storage, potentially allowing data to be altered or corrupted during the teacher's grade entry process.
assumptions: Assumes the system should implement data integrity checks and encryption.

title: Unintended data exposure
description: The Grades Portal Web App may inadvertently expose student grades and feedback to unauthorized users through improper data handling, such as insufficient data masking or improper field-level access controls.
assumptions: Assumes the system should implement proper data masking and field-level access controls.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records
description: Grade records containing student identifiers, grades, and feedback may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is not properly secured or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Unauthorized modification of grade records
description: Grade records may be modified by unauthorized actors if the data store lacks proper integrity controls or if the process does not validate data before writing.

title: Loss or destruction of grade records
description: Grade records may be lost or destroyed due to data store corruption, deletion, or system failure, resulting in permanent loss of student academic records.

title: Unavailability of grade records
description: Grade records may become unavailable when needed due to data store failures, network issues, or maintenance activities, preventing timely access to student grades.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes the student's request for their own grades and feedback, which involves handling identified personal data. There is a risk that the system may process this data in ways that exceed the student's authorization or intended use.
assumptions: The system correctly identifies the student and their request is legitimate.

title: Linking of student request to other data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may link the student's grade request to other data in the system, potentially creating unintended associations or profiles that could be used for purposes beyond the student's original intent.
assumptions: The system does not have mechanisms to link requests to other data sources.

title: Unintended consequences of data processing
description: Processing the student's grade request may have unintended consequences, such as affecting the student's academic record, creating audit trails, or triggering other system actions that were not anticipated by the student.
assumptions: The system processes requests in isolation without triggering side effects.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades display
description: Unauthorized users may access the student's grades and teacher feedback through the portal without proper authentication controls, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized parties.

title: Information leakage during display
description: The grades and feedback may be displayed in a manner that could inadvertently expose information to unauthorized viewers (e.g., through screen sharing, browser history, or improper display settings).

title: Data integrity during display
description: The grades and feedback displayed to the student may be tampered with or altered before presentation, potentially showing incorrect or manipulated information.

title: Unauthorized Parent Access to Child's Grades
description: Parent (EE2) may access child's grades without proper authentication or authorization controls, potentially allowing unauthorized individuals to view sensitive educational information.

title: Parent Access to Other Children's Grades
description: Parent account may be linked to multiple children, allowing parent to access grades for children they are not authorized to view, violating privacy boundaries.

title: Parent Credentials Interception
description: Parent's login credentials transmitted from EE2 to P1 may be intercepted during transmission, compromising authentication security.

title: Child's Grades Data Tampering
description: Grades data stored in the system may be modified or corrupted without proper integrity controls, affecting accuracy of educational records.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades to unauthorized parents
description: Parent portal may allow access to student grades by individuals who are not the actual legal guardians or authorized parents, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized access to grades portal by malicious actors
description: Malicious actors may attempt to gain unauthorized access to the grades portal to view or manipulate student academic records, feedback, and submission history.

title: Data loss during transmission to parent
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may be lost or corrupted during transmission from the portal to the parent's device or network, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate information.

title: Unintended exposure of sensitive student information
description: Parents may inadvertently access information they do not need or understand, such as detailed feedback or submission history, potentially causing confusion or inappropriate responses.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Parental access to student grades and academic records may not fully comply with GDPR or other data protection regulations regarding consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation.

title: Lack of Authentication for Administrator Access
description: School Administrator (EE4) may access the Grades Portal Web App (P1) without proper authentication, allowing unauthorized individuals to perform account management operations.
assumptions: Administrator identity is not verified before system access

title: Inadequate Access Controls for Account Management
description: The system may not have sufficient access controls to restrict account creation, modification, and disabling operations to only authorized administrators, potentially allowing unauthorized personnel to manipulate student data.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced

title: Data Integrity Risk During Account Modifications
description: Administrator actions to create, modify, or disable accounts and parent-child links may result in data integrity issues if the system does not properly validate input data or maintain audit trails.
assumptions: Input validation and audit logging are not fully implemented

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Student Information
description: Administrator actions may inadvertently expose sensitive student information (names, emails, relationships) to unauthorized parties if access controls or data transmission security are inadequate.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage security measures are insufficient

title: Unintended Data Flow During Account Operations
description: Account management operations may result in unintended data flows where sensitive information is transmitted to unauthorized destinations or stored in unexpected locations.
assumptions: Data flow paths are not fully mapped or controlled

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: Account records containing sensitive user information (e.g., student identifiers, grades, parent-child relationships) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the write operation to the account directory.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory is accessible to unauthorized actors

title: Loss of Account Records During Write Operation
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links could be lost or corrupted during the write operation to the account directory, resulting in data integrity issues.
assumptions: Assumes the write operation may fail or be interrupted

title: Unintended Consequences of Account Data Write
description: The write operation could have unintended consequences, such as writing incorrect, incomplete, or outdated account records to the directory.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service may not always write accurate data

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The write operation to the account directory may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding the handling of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service handles personal data without explicit compliance measures

title: Unnecessary transfer of personal data to third-party cloud provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider. This may violate the minimality principle if data is shared beyond what is strictly required for the backup/replication purpose.
assumptions: The transfer is necessary for backup purposes, but the scope of data shared may exceed requirements.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the full data scope is necessary for the stated backup purpose.

title: Implicit data disclosure through metadata
description: The transfer of grade records and account directory to third-party cloud provider may result in implicit disclosure of personal data through metadata or derived information that could be inferred from the transferred data.
assumptions: Third-party cloud provider may retain, process, or infer additional information from the transferred data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the extent of data processing by the third-party provider.

title: Unauthorized access to personal data by third-party provider
description: The third-party cloud hosting provider may have unauthorized or excessive access to the personal data (grade records, assignments, account directory) stored on their infrastructure.
assumptions: The third-party provider may have employees or systems with access to the data beyond what is necessary for hosting services.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the third-party provider's security controls and access management practices.

title: Data leakage during transfer to third-party provider
description: Personal data transferred from the Assignment & Grading Service to the cloud hosting provider may be intercepted, leaked, or exposed during the transfer process.
assumptions: The transfer may not be adequately protected against interception or unauthorized access during transit.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the security measures in place for data in transit.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records to unauthorized parties
description: Grade records may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems without proper authentication and authorization controls, potentially exposing sensitive student academic information to individuals who should not have access.

title: Inadequate access controls on grade records
description: Access controls on the grade records data store may be insufficient to prevent unauthorized access, with potential for data disclosure to unauthorized users or systems.

title: Lack of data encryption for grade records in transit
description: Grade records may not be encrypted during transmission from the data store to the grading service, potentially exposing sensitive student information during data transfer.

title: Lack of audit logging for data access
description: There may be no audit logging mechanism to track who accessed grade records and when, making it difficult to detect unauthorized access or data breaches.

title: Inadequate data minimization in grade record processing
description: The grading service may process more data than necessary for building student, parent, and teacher views, potentially exposing more information than required.

title: Unintended data exposure to third-party systems
description: Grade records may be inadvertently exposed to third-party systems or services that should not have access to student academic information.
